steps.title: Whites
steps.body: About 80% of Friuli's wine is white. Friulano, formerly Tocai Friulano, gives full, almond-scented whites; it was renamed in 2008 after the EU protected Hungary's Tokaji name. Ribolla Gialla gives crisp, citrus whites and is key to orange wines. Pinot Grigio, Sauvignon Blanc and Chardonnay are widely grown.

steps.title: Reds and sweet wines
steps.body: Reds include Refosco dal Peduncolo Rosso, dark and tart; Schioppettino, peppery and fragrant; and Pignolo, tannic. Merlot and Cabernet Franc are also grown. Picolit, a sweet white, made from dried grapes, was once famous at European courts; Ramandolo is another sweet white, from Verduzzo.

steps.prompt: Match each grape to its style.
steps.explanation: Friuli grows native and international grapes.

steps.body: Friulano was called Tocai until 2008. Old bottles and older Italian drinkers may still use the name.

options: The EU protected Hungary's Tokaji name
